Staying Connected to Support When You Are Between Homes

Being between Brisbane homes can throw everything up in the air. You might be moving suburbs, building, renovating, staying with family, or dealing with a tricky rental situation. Even if the move is positive, it can still shake your sleep, your patience, your routines and your closest relationships.

Mental health does not pause just because you are surrounded by boxes. In fact, times of change often bring buried worries to the surface. Old anxiety, low mood, trauma responses, eating struggles or relationship tensions can feel louder when the rest of life feels unsettled. Telehealth counselling offers a way to keep steady support in place, even when you are living out of suitcases or driving between properties in peak traffic or wet weather.

Telehealth sessions can fit around school holidays, new work hours and the winter cold and flu season, when leaving the house might feel extra hard. We aim to help you stay supported and grounded, no matter where your temporary bedroom or kitchen table may be this week.

Why Life Between Homes Can Feel so Overwhelming

Moving is often described as one of the most stressful life events, and there are good reasons for that. When you are between homes, you may feel:

  • Anxiety about the unknown, such as new suburbs, schools or workplaces
  • Grief about leaving a familiar street, church or neighbours
  • Pressure in your relationship, with more snappy arguments or silence
  • Worry about money, timelines and things going wrong

When routines are disrupted, everything can feel harder. Simple things like:

  • Regular sleep and wake times
  • Meal planning and eating well
  • Exercise or movement habits
  • Spiritual practices like prayer, Bible reading or church involvement
  • Catch-ups with friends and family

can all get pushed aside by packing, cleaning and paperwork. For someone already dealing with anxiety, depression, trauma, eating disorders or relationship conflict, this loss of rhythm can increase symptoms or make coping strategies harder to use.

In Brisbane, there are extra pressures too. A tight rental market, long travel times between old and new suburbs and periods in temporary accommodation can all add stress. Getting to a face-to-face appointment across the city can feel almost impossible right when you most need support.

How Telehealth Counselling Can Support You Through Moving

Telehealth counselling means meeting with a qualified clinical psychologist through secure video or phone instead of in the therapy room. You can attend from wherever you are staying, whether that is a relative’s spare room, a short-term rental, or your half-renovated new place. As long as you have a phone or device and a decent connection, your support can come to you.

Some of the main benefits when you are between homes include:

  • No travel time through traffic, storms or unfamiliar suburbs
  • Easier planning around removalists, inspections and school runs
  • Ability to keep working with the same psychologist even if you change suburbs or move further away
  • More flexibility if you are sharing cars, looking after kids or juggling work changes

Privacy and comfort matter too. Between homes, you might feel you have less control over your space. Some simple ideas can help you feel safer to speak honestly:

  • Choose the quietest room or corner available, even if it is the car in the driveway
  • Use headphones so others cannot overhear your psychologist
  • Let family or housemates know you will be on a private call and need not to be disturbed
  • Have a blanket, cup of tea or favourite jumper nearby to help your body feel settled

Our goal in telehealth is the same as in person: a safe, kind and steady space where you can speak freely about stress, conflict, faith and decision making.

Practical Tips to Get the Most From Online Sessions

Telehealth counselling does not need to be complicated. A little preparation can help your sessions feel calmer and more focused.

For the practical setup, it helps to:

  • Check your phone or laptop is charged and your internet or data is working
  • Pick a spot with comfortable seating and enough light for video
  • Have tissues, water and a notebook or notes app close by
  • Log in or be ready for the phone call a few minutes early, so you are not rushing straight from packing or cleaning

Emotional readiness is just as important. Before your session, it can help to pause and gently ask yourself:

  • What has been the hardest part of this week?
  • Where have I felt most stressed, upset or stuck?
  • What did I want to say to someone but kept inside?

You might jot down a few dot points, such as sleep troubles, parenting worries, fears about money, or spiritual questions about what God is doing in this season. In your session, you and your psychologist can agree on small, realistic steps to try between appointments, like one calming practice at bedtime or one new way to communicate in your relationship.

For couples and families, telehealth can be very flexible:

  • Parents can have sessions focused on supporting children or teens with school changes or leaving friends
  • Children can attend online with a parent nearby if that feels safer
  • Couples can join together from the same room, or from separate locations if space or tension makes that easier

The aim is to keep everyone as supported as possible, even if the family is spread between different houses or suburbs for a while.

Faith, Values and Continuity of Care While You Move

For many people, moving affects spiritual rhythms as well as emotional ones. You might be changing churches, stepping back from small groups, or feeling unsure where you fit in a new community. Christian counselling and values-aligned therapy can provide steady spiritual support during this in-between time.

Telehealth means your faith conversations do not have to stop just because your regular church routine is changing. You can keep exploring questions such as:

  • How do we make wise choices for our family in this move?
  • What might calling and purpose look like in a new suburb or role?
  • How do we stay grounded in faith when everything else feels temporary?

At Michelle Barratt Psychology in Brisbane, we take a holistic approach, paying attention to emotional, relational and spiritual wellbeing. Whether you are seen in person or through telehealth counselling, our focus is on compassionate, evidence-based care for concerns like anxiety, depression, trauma, eating difficulties, relationship issues and life transitions.

Taking the Next Step Toward Steadier Ground

It can be tempting to put off support until the move is finished, the boxes are unpacked, and life feels normal again. In reality, early support can make a big difference, lowering the chance that stress will grow into more serious mental health difficulties for you, your partner or your family.

If you are between Brisbane homes and feeling stretched thin, telehealth counselling can give you a stable point in the week, a regular time to breathe, reflect and be guided. At Michelle Barratt Psychology, we offer Telehealth options alongside face-to-face sessions, and where appropriate, some sessions may be eligible for Medicare rebates. Even while you are between addresses, it is possible to start building a sense of stability, one conversation at a time.

Take The Next Step Toward Personal Support and Clarity

If you are feeling ready to talk through what is going on and explore new ways of coping, we are here to help at Michelle Barratt Psychology. Our telehealth counselling sessions make it easier to access support in a way that fits with your daily life. Reach out to contact us, and we can discuss your needs and help you book a time that feels right for you. Together, we will work at your pace toward meaningful and sustainable change.
